paper_title: Solving Target Set Selection with Bounded Thresholds Faster than 2^n
classifications: Theory of computation → Graph algorithms analysis
Theory of computation → Parameterized complexity and exact algorithms
statement: If v ∈ Z, at this point, we cannot compute the number of activated neighbours of v exactly as we do not know what neighbours of v are in B. Note that we do not need the exact number of such neighbours if we know that this value is at least thr(v). Thus we branch into thr(v) + 1 subbranches corresponding to the value of min{|N (v) ∩ B|, thr(v)}, from now on we denote this value as dg(v).
context: If v ∈ B, the decision for v does not matter. Thus if v ∈ F and |N (v) ∩ Pi | < thr(v), we may simply not include v in Pi+1 . If v ∈ Z, at this point, we cannot compute the number of activated neighbours of v exactly as we do not know what neighbours of v are in B. Note that we do not need the exact number of such neighbours if we know that this value is at least thr(v). Thus we branch into thr(v) + 1 subbranches corresponding to the value of min{|N (v) ∩ B|, thr(v)}, from now on we denote this value as dg(v). On the other hand, we know all activated neighbours of v that are in V (G) \ F since Si (X) ∩ (V (G) \ F ) = Pi ∩ (V (G) \ F ), as B ⊆ F . Let this number be m = |N (v) ∩ (Pi \ F )|. So the number of activated neighbours of v is at least m + dg(v). Also there may be some activated neighbours of v in N (v) ∩ Pi ∩ F . However, we cannot simply add |N (v) ∩ Pi ∩ F | to m + dg(v) since vertices in Pi ∩ B will be computed twice. So we are actually interested in the value of |(N (v) ∩ Pi ∩ F ) \ B|. That is why for vertices from N (v) ∩ Pi ∩ F we simply branch whether they are in B or not. After that we compare m + dg(v) + |(N (v) ∩ Pi ∩ F ) \ B| with thr(v) and figure out whether v becomes activated in the current round or not. Note that once we branch on the value of min{|N (v) ∩ B|, thr(v)}, or on whether v ∈ B or not for some v, we will not branch on the same value or make a decision for the same vertex again as it makes no sense. Once fixed, the decision should not change along the whole branch and all of its subbranches, otherwise the information about B would just become inconsistent.
